sentences: That's how long you stay awake in space without a suit.
In nineteen sixty-six, a NASA test subject named Jim LeBlanc found out the hard way.
His suit lost pressure inside a vacuum chamber.
First, the air rushes out of your lungs.
Then the saliva on your tongue starts to boil.
LeBlanc said he could feel it bubbling.
Your blood vessels keep it under pressure.
Blood with no oxygen reaches your brain, and the lights go out.
LeBlanc passed out in fourteen seconds.
They repressurized the chamber, and he woke up fine.
Fourteen seconds. That's all you get.
